0.name: Zero Property of Multiplication
0.student_tip: Any number multiplied by 0 is always 0! Imagine 5 empty bags—you have 0 items.

1.name: Identity Property of Multiplication
1.student_tip: Any number multiplied by 1 stays the exact same number! 1 group of 8 is just 8.

2.name: Doubles Strategy
2.student_tip: Multiplying by 2 is just doubling the other number! (e.g., 2 × 6 is 6 + 6 = 12).

3.name: Double Plus One Group
3.student_tip: To multiply by 3, double the number first, then add one more group! (3 × 7 = 14 + 7 = 21).

4.name: Double and Double Again
4.student_tip: To multiply by 4, double the number, then double it again! (4 × 6: double 6 is 12, double 12 is 24!).

5.name: Clock / Half-of-Ten Strategy
5.student_tip: Multiplying by 5 always ends in 0 or 5. Think of the minute hand on a clock or half of 10!
5.visual_hint: Skip-count by 5s or take half of (10 × n)

6.name: Five Plus One Group (or Double 3s)
6.student_tip: To multiply by 6, find the 5s fact first, then add one more group! (6 × 7 = (5 × 7) + 7 = 35 + 7 = 42).

8.name: Double-Double-Double
8.student_tip: To multiply by 8, double three times! Or think: 8 × n = (5 × n) + (3 × n).

9.name: Ten Minus One Group (or Digits Sum to 9)
9.student_tip: To multiply by 9, multiply by 10 first and subtract 1 group! (9 × 6 = 60 - 6 = 54. Notice 5 + 4 = 9!).

10.name: Place-Value Shift
10.student_tip: Multiplying by 10 shifts the digits one place value to the left (ends in a zero).

11.name: Ten Plus One Group
11.student_tip: To multiply by 11, multiply by 10 first, then add one more group! (11 × 4 = 40 + 4 = 44).
